experiment: Reduce the LLMD --batch-size from its default of 16 to 1, matching the genuinely serial decode stream in the frozen development profile.
hypothesis: The measured workload is strictly serial: six small prompts x five repeats, one request in flight at a time, 14-27 input tokens, short greedy (temperature 0, top_k 1) decodes. Both prior measured candidates were no_change -- page-chunk-size 16->64 and prefill-chunk-size 256->1024 -- and the latter was a nonbinding input-token threshold (every input is < 256, so it never split a prefill chunk). --batch-size is a concurrency/batching cap, not a token-count threshold: it is the documented 'Maximum concurrent request batch size'. Capping it at 1 aligns the engine's max-batch provisioning with the real serial concurrency, so no 16-way decode batch is provisioned, allocated, or scheduled per serial request; the mechanism can trim per-request TTFT and decode-step overhead on the serial stream. Because the stream never exceeds one in-flight request, capping at 1 cannot regress correctness or cause queuing.
notes: Exactly one documented LLMD CMD flag changes: --batch-size 16 -> 1 ('Maximum concurrent request batch size (default: 16)' per llmd --help). Every other CMD flag and all other Dockerfile bytes are preserved verbatim: --io-impl=zio, --token-batch-size=1024, --max-context-len=128000, --prefill-chunk-size=256, --page-chunk-size=16, --backend=auto, --gpu-memory-fraction=0.9, --cache-memory-fraction=0.95; the ARG/FROM base image pin, the commented-out ENV telemetry lines, and ENTRYPOINT [/llmd/llmd] are unchanged. No RUN steps, no extra weights, tokenizer, quantization, chat-template, backend, model, download, credential, or egress changes; no benchmark, golden, greedy, measurement, prompt, or cached-answer changes. This deliberately avoids the rejected categories: it is not an input-token threshold knob (prefill-chunk-size / token-batch-size / max-context-len, all of which sit above the 14-27 token usage and would not bind), not a GPU-only backend (cuda_fa2/fa3/mosaic_tpu fail with no GPU, and triton likely equals or regresses auto on CPU), not the unavailable native DFlash drafter, and not the greedy-overridden --topk. As the stream is already effectively single-concurrency, the dominant likely outcome is no_change; no measured speedup or gain is claimed. Startup is unchanged in kind (no new assets, backend, or model). These are supplied development decisions, not an official grade.
risk: Low. The profile is explicitly serial, so the actual in-flight concurrency is 1, which the cap of 1 satisfies exactly: no request is queued or refused, so all six correctness gates remain satisfiable and startup is unaffected (no new model, backend, or egress). The expected downside is no_change if the engine provisions per active sequence rather than per max-batch cap; no throughput regression is expected because the active decode batch is already one. No measured gain is asserted; root will build and measure later on currently GPU-absent hardware.
